erection of Wing at St. Bruno's Indian School


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 16, 1924.

SIR, - Cheque No. 6370 issued in March last and charged against the vote for Indian Education is for the payment of
$10,775.85 to Rev. C. Falher, O.M.I., as a grant towards the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Indian Residential School
which was destroyed by fire during the winter of 1923 - 24.

According to the vouchers submitted in support of this payment, your department, with the approval of the
Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, offered the Bishop of Athabasca a grant of $12,000 towards the rebuilding.
The church authorities were to be responsible for the labour on the building and were to present receipted accounts for
the material purchased and for the freighting. The payment in question represents the receipted accounts that have been
presented, but a number of the receipted accounts attached to the vouchers indicate the total amount paid, without
giving any particulars as to the quantity and prices of the materials furnished.

I am of opinion that the authority of the Governor in Council should have been obtained before an expenditure of this
nature was incurred.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, June 24, 1924.

DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 16th instant with reference to the payment
by this Department of a grant toward



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 569-572) ===
<!-- page 569 -->
the erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School. I have noted for future reference your opinion that the authority
of the Governor in Council should be obtained before expenditures of this nature are incurred.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, June 26, 1924.

SIR, - I am in receipt of your letter of the 24th inst., replying to mine of the 16th with reference to a grant towards the
erection of a wing at St. Bruno's Boarding School.

In your reply you state that you have noted for future reference my opinion that the authority of the Governor in
Council should be obtained before expenditures of this nature are incurred.

While my previous letter did not so definitely state, still it was intended to express my opinion, not only that all future
payments of a like nature should be authorized by the Governor in Council, but also that such authority should be
obtained for the particular payment in question. I have accordingly to request that you take the necessary steps to
obtain the approval of the Governor in Council to this grant to St. Bruno's School.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Purchase of Round Lake Residential School from Presbyterian Church in Canada


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, October 6, 1924.

Sir, - Cheque No. 6,133 of 1923 - 24, vote for Indian Education, is for a payment of $8,000 to the Treasurer of the
Presbyterian Church in Canada for the purchase of the Round Lake Indian Residential School, which was the property
of the Presbyterian Church, but, on which over $18,000 had been spent for repairs, etc., during the last two fiscal years.

I am of the opinion that, the authority of the Governor in Council should have been obtained for the purchase of this
property. Kindly let me know what valuation was placed on the property at the time of purchase, and by whom such
valuation was made.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, October 17, 1924.

<!-- page 570 -->
DEAR MR. KEARNS, - I have your letter of the 6th instant, with reference to Indian Education cheque No. 6433,
being a payment of $8,000 to the Presbyterian Church for the Round Lake Indian Residential School property which
was transferred to the Crown.

<!-- page 571 -->
In reply I have to inform you that the Presbyterian Church in November 1922, suggested a nominal price of $10,000 or
$12,000 for the church property at the school. As was explained on the voucher, the property consisted of
approximately 22 acres on which was situated the residential school, the barns and other outbuildings. The buildings
alone represented an investment on the part of the Church of considerably more than either of these figures. The land is
entirely in the valley and is quite valuable.

In the winter of 1923 - 24, a fire destroyed the classroom, which was one of the outbuildings. I learned that insurance,
amounting to $2,000 was paid to the Church authorities. I immediately suggested that this amount be deducted from
their lowest price and that the consideration for the property be $8,000. I discussed the question with
Mr. Commissioner Graham, who is thoroughly familiar with the situation, and he considered this a fair adjustment and
a satisfactory price.


Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.

Vote 279, Indian Education: Payment in Advance of Salary of Truant Officer


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, October 27, 1924.

SIR, - Cheque No. 587, issued on April 30, 1923, and changed against the vote for Indian Education is for the payment
of $80 to Matt Bernard, being payment in advance of his salary of Truant Officer and Caretaker of the Golden Lake
school for the fiscal year 1923 - 24.

Kindly advise me of the circumstances under which this man's salary was paid in advance for the full fiscal year, and
of your authority for making Such payment in advance. Payment for services should be made only at the end of regular
periods, such as monthly or quarterly, and then only for such services as have been actually rendered at the time of
making payment. The only exception to this rule is the case of the permanent employees at Ottawa who are paid their
salaries at the middle instead of at the end of each month under special authority.


I am, Sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, October 29, 1924.

DEAR SIR, - I have your letter of the 27th instant with reference to an advance made to Matt Bernard of his salary as
Truant Officer and Caretaker of the Golden Lake school for the last fiscal year.

Mr. Bernard is Chief of the Band, and has been for several years acting in the capacity of Truant Officer and Caretaker
for the school. Having confidence in his reliability the Department made the advance in question to enable him to carry
out some building operations in connection with a lot which he had acquired on the reserve. Had this not been done
the Department might have been under obligation to make a loan to the Chief.

The services, covered by this payment have been fully and satisfactorily rendered.

<!-- page 572 -->
Yours very truly,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Assistant Auditor General.
